summary.headline: Bharat Parenterals FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose to INR 15.8 crores from INR 2.7 crores, driven by Innoxel's loss narrowing; standalone revenue fell 23% to INR 234 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was broadly flat at INR 345.4 crores versus INR 340 crores, but the mix shifted: standalone BPL revenue fell about 23% to INR 234 crores on deferred export tenders, exits from low-margin volume and about two months of production downtime for upgrades. Innoxel's revenue rose 174% to INR 72.4 crores, its EBITDA loss narrowed by INR 23.5 crores, and it turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26 (INR 1.4 crores). Varenyam Healthcare grew 13.7% to INR 58.4 crores and turned profitable. FY27 guidance is given by business: standalone 10-15% growth, Innoxel 35-45% growth, and Varenyam 20-25% growth, with management conceding the standalone base will only partially recover this year.

segments.name: BPL standalone (exports, injectables)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 234 crores (down about 23%), EBITDA INR 21 crores at 9% margin; capacity utilisation 48% general, 21% beta-lactam, 24% cephalosporins; order book INR 171 crores.

segments.name: Innoxel Lifesciences (complex generics/CDMO, US/EU)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 72.4 crores (up 174%), EBITDA loss INR 6.9 crores; US FDA establishment inspection report received and EUGMP clearance from FAMHP with zero critical and zero major observations; 19 active partners and 42 assets in pipeline.

segments.name: Varenyam Healthcare (domestic branded)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 58.4 crores (up 13.7%), EBITDA INR 2.5 crores and PAT INR 2.3 crores; 45 active brands, top five brands INR 28.7 crores (about half of revenue); Sugammadex over INR 10 crores; PCPM up 31% YoY to over INR 3.85 lakh.

segments.name: Varenyam Biolifesciences (pre-revenue)
segments.commentary: Facility under construction with approved budget about INR 160 crores and CWIP about INR 33 crores (around 20% complete); commissioning targeted September 2027, first EUGMP filing Q1 FY29, first commercial supply Q4 FY29.

guidance_outlook: Standalone BPL: revenue growth 10-15% and EBITDA margin 10-15% in FY27; management expects only partial recovery this year, with full recovery to FY25 levels targeted in FY28.

Innoxel: revenue growth 35-45% and EBITDA margin 20-25% in FY27; first commercial CMO supply from Q2 FY27, two to three CMO products commercialising in the year, 10 new filings, 20 new partner deals targeted, out-licensing income INR 70-90 crores, first MHRA and Health Canada filings.
Varenyam Healthcare: revenue growth 20-25% and EBITDA margin 8-13% in FY27; field force to exceed 250, seven product launches including Remishot, and launch of a gynecology division.
Varenyam Biolifesciences: commissioning of manufacturing lines by September 2027 and validation by March 2028; remains pre-revenue through FY27.
Standalone peak revenue of INR 400-500 crores expected on a 2030 horizon, sequential over 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: BPL standalone utilisation is low (48% general, 21% beta-lactam, 24% cephalosporins); management says 10-15% growth is possible without fresh capex.
Upgrades to the general injectable vial line, beta-lactam water system and structural changes for EUGMP ran through FY26, costing about two months of production across all three blocks.
PIC/S and EUGMP inspections at standalone facilities are scheduled during FY27 and are expected to cause some disruption before certification.
Innoxel's facility is validated and cleared for commercial supply to the US and selected European markets; new capacity depreciation is weighing on PAT.
Varenyam Biolifesciences: CWIP about INR 33 crores against budget of about INR 160 crores; civil works 50% complete, equipment procurement about 40%.
demand_pricing: BPL order book of INR 171 crores gives FY27 visibility; growth is expected from Southeast Asia, Africa and MENA.

A $27 million tender order (Jan 2025 announcement) was delayed; orders were received in early March 2026, supply has started, and about 90% is expected to be covered in FY27 with small spillover into early FY28.
BPL filings: 214 dossiers submitted, 40 new product registrations across Africa, LATAM and Southeast Asia, over 350 live filings in more than 40 countries; Vietnam representative office opened.
Varenyam corporate hospital coverage is over 7,500 institutions across 26 states; 50 new corporate hospital tie-ups added in FY26; medical sales force grew from 190 to 211.

Innoxel: two 505(b)(2) assets (exhibit batches done, on stability) targeted for US filing in Q3 and Q4 FY27 under partner names; one asset is filed or partly filed in Europe, with filing planned later this month.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 standalone guidance of 10-15% growth on a base of about INR 230-250 crores rather than INR 300 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the base is FY26 revenue. It expects partial recovery in FY27, with disruption from PIC/S and EUGMP preparation and inspections, and full recovery to FY25 levels in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is standalone peak revenue INR 400-500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 400-500 crores is the target for the standalone business, but sequentially over 3-4 years, with peak revenue framed from a 2030 standpoint.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Varenyam Bio's commercialisation timeline moved from 2027 to Q4 FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project is running at least one quarter behind schedule, citing geopolitical disruption. Filing now starts around Q1 FY28, first EUGMP filing is Q1 FY29, and commercial supply is Q4 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY27 guidances cut across segments, especially Varenyam?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier guidance was not met, so the new ranges are softer and deliberately achievable. Varenyam's earlier INR 75-80 crore revenue ambition was not restated; FY27 growth is 20-25% with heavy investment in field force and a new division.

qa_highlights.question: What drives Innoxel's FY27 margin expansion, and how much is CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from milestone payments and fixed cost leverage. Commercial supply is limited to two or at most three products. Management would not quantify CDMO revenue share, saying own-product manufacturing revenue starts in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing of the two Innoxel 505(b)(2) assets and the CMO commercialisations?
qa_highlights.answer: The two 505(b)(2) assets are targeted for US filing in Q3 and Q4 FY27, filed in partner names. One CMO product commercialises in Q2 FY27 and a second between Q3 and Q4 FY27; Innoxel earns fees and milestones rather than profit share on CMO deals.

risks_watch: Standalone BPL: FY27 growth of 10-15% is on an FY26 base of about INR 234 crores, with partial recovery expected; PIC/S and EUGMP inspections in FY27 may cause production disruption before certification.

Varenyam Biolifesciences: commissioning slipped to September 2027 with first commercial supply now Q4 FY29; management cited geopolitical disruption and at least one quarter of delay; approved budget about INR 160 crores with CWIP about INR 33 crores, so funding and cash needs warrant tracking.

Innoxel FY27 margin expansion (20-25%) relies largely on milestone payments and fixed-cost leverage; management did not quantify the CDMO revenue share and own-product manufacturing revenue starts only in FY28.
Out-licensing income guidance of INR 70-90 crores and 20 new partner deals are large against the FY26 Innoxel revenue of INR 72.4 crores; deal conversion is a key monitorable.

Varenyam Healthcare investment ramp (field force above 250, a new gynecology division, seven launches) may keep margins compressed; top five brands are about half of revenue and Sugammadex is about 17.5% of company revenue.
key_quotes: We'd rather give you ranges we are confident in than point estimates we have to walk back.
this time around the guidances have been on the softer side and it is something that we feel is very, that we are very confident of achieving these guidances.

The total number is something that I will not be able to give at this moment, but it would take, this is a topic that can be discussed maybe later through the year when there is some more clarity in terms of regulatory and in terms of approval timelines that we get from the FDA and from our partners.
There would be some sort of disruption coming from these two inspections for this year.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on Innoxel regulatory clearances and the Q4 EBITDA turn, but cautious and somewhat defensive on standalone recovery and FY27 guidance, which it said was deliberately set softer after earlier guidance was missed. It was evasive on quantifying Innoxel's CDMO revenue share and Varenyam's earlier INR 75-80 crore revenue ambition, which it did not restate.

adds.what: Varenyam Biolifesciences pre-revenue manufacturing facility (approved budget ~INR 160 crore, ~20% complete)

growth.why: FY27 guidance is standalone 10-15%, Innoxel 35-45% and Varenyam 20-25% revenue growth; standalone has a 171 crore order book and 48% utilisation with no fresh capex needed, while Innoxel and Varenyam growth rest on partner deals, filings and launches rather than new capacity.
